dataflow.heading: Data flow
dataflow.step1: The recorder sends audio to the company's own Cloudflare account. R2 audio storage uses EU jurisdiction; Durable Objects upload sessions use jurisdiction eu. Both are available without Enterprise.
dataflow.step2: {provider} receives audio and keyterms directly and returns text and speakers.
dataflow.step3: The configured language model writes the recap from the transcript, with requests passing through AI Gateway. Meeting data is stored in D1.
dataflow.step4: Audio is deleted after {audioDays, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Transcripts and recaps are deleted after {textDays, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Keep prevents both deletions.
dataflow.promise: Processing is not guaranteed to stay in the EU.
dataflow.caveats: D1 has no jurisdiction setting. Worker placement is best effort, normally at the data centre nearest the request; regional restrictions require the Enterprise-only Data Localization Suite. Workers AI and AI Gateway are not covered by Regional Services.
dataflow.local: A local live transcript stays on the computer and is discarded when the meeting ends. After the server confirms a recording, the recorder keeps the audio locally for 7 days. Without a confirmation it keeps the file and retries.
